groups.name: Acyl Halides & Acid Chlorides
groups.description: Highly reactive organic acid halides (e.g., Sebacoyl chloride, Acetyl chloride) that undergo violent nucleophilic acyl substitution.

groups.name: Halogenated Organic Compounds
groups.description: Chlorinated/brominated hydrocarbons (e.g., Dichloromethane, Chloroform) sensitive to active metals and caustics; persistent environmental toxins.

groups.name: Water-Reactive Substances
groups.description: Substances that react violently with moisture, generating toxic/corrosive gases or intense exothermic heat.

groups.name: Water & Aqueous Solutions
groups.description: Water, aqueous buffers, saline, and water-based pharmaceutical formulations.

groups.name: Strong Oxidizing Agents
groups.description: Electron acceptors (e.g., Hydrogen peroxide, Nitric acid, Potassium permanganate) capable of causing runaway combustion with organics.

groups.name: Strong Reducing Agents
groups.description: Substances (e.g., Sodium borohydride, Hydrides, Sulfites) that release flammable hydrogen or react violently with oxidizers.

groups.name: Inorganic / Mineral Acids
groups.description: Strong mineral acids (e.g., Hydrochloric acid, Sulfuric acid, Phosphoric acid) that violently neutralize bases.

groups.name: Organic / Carboxylic Acids
groups.description: Carbon-based acids (e.g., Acetic acid, Citric acid, Formic acid) that react exothermically with bases and amines.

groups.name: Caustics & Strong Bases
groups.description: Alkaline compounds (e.g., Sodium hydroxide, Potassium hydroxide, Ammonia) that react violently with acids and acyl halides.

groups.name: Alcohols & Polyols
groups.description: Hydroxy compounds (e.g., Ethanol, Isopropanol, Methanol, Glycerol) susceptible to rapid esterification and flammability.

groups.name: Amines & Nitrogenous Bases
groups.description: Organic amines and amino compounds (e.g., Triethylamine, Piperidine, APIs with amine motifs) acting as nucleophiles.

groups.name: Cyanides & Nitriles
groups.description: Cyanide salts and organic nitriles capable of releasing lethal Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) gas under acidic conditions.

groups.name: Sulfides & Mercaptans
groups.description: Sulfur-containing reagents that generate toxic, asphyxiating Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) gas when exposed to acids.

groups.name: Peroxides & Hydroperoxides
groups.description: Unstable O-O bond compounds prone to friction/heat-induced explosive deflagration and violent oxidation.

groups.name: Flammable & Combustible Solvents
groups.description: Low-flashpoint organic solvents (e.g., Acetone, Hexane, Ethyl acetate, Ethanol) presenting vapor ignition hazards.

groups.name: Cytotoxic & Antineoplastic Agents
groups.description: Genotoxic, mutagenic, or teratogenic antineoplastic pharmaceuticals (e.g., Cisplatin, Methotrexate, Doxorubicin) governed by USP <800>.

matrix.description: Acyl halides react violently and exothermically with water or aqueous drug solutions, generating dense, choking Hydrogen Chloride (HCl) acid vapor and boiling corrosive spray. High risk of vessel overpressurization.
matrix.segregationAction: Store strictly under desiccated/dry conditions. NEVER dispose into aqueous waste sinks or wet carboys. Collect in dedicated anhydrous fluoropolymer/PTFE carboys for high-temperature hazardous waste incineration (>1200°C).

matrix.description: Co-storing multiple water-reactive substances compounds the fire, thermal runaway, and toxic acid gas generation risk upon any atmospheric seal breach.
matrix.segregationAction: Isolate in an airtight desiccator cabinet with secondary containment and inert nitrogen blanket.

matrix.description: Mixing strong bases with acyl halides causes an immediate, explosive exothermic runaway. The heat of reaction can boil solvents instantly and shatter glass vessels.
matrix.segregationAction: Strict segregation into non-compatible waste streams. Neutralization must only be conducted in a controlled, ice-cooled jacketed reactor under slow stoichiometric addition.

matrix.description: Spontaneous reaction between acyl halides and alcohols generates ester compounds with intense heat and rapid evolution of anhydrous Hydrogen Chloride gas, causing severe pressure buildup in closed waste drums.
matrix.segregationAction: Separate acyl halides completely from organic solvent/alcohol waste drums. Ensure waste drum has a pressure-relief safety cap.

matrix.description: Vigorous nucleophilic attack by amines on acyl chlorides liberates immense heat, amine hydrochloride salt precipitate, and aerosolized toxic amine vapors.
matrix.segregationAction: Collect amine-containing API waste separately from acid chlorides. Keep in segregated flammables/bases cabinet.

matrix.description: Mixing mineral acids and strong caustics triggers instant, extreme thermal discharge capable of boiling the liquid mixture, causing caustic steam eruptions and thermal burns.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in separate, dedicated, corrosion-proof polypropylene cabinets (Blue = Acids, Red/White = Bases). Do not co-mingle in neutralization sumps without automated pH chilling controls.

matrix.description: Rapid acid-base reaction generating significant heat. May cause volatile organic acid fumes to vaporize into the breathing zone.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate organic acids from caustic solutions. Dilute slowly before any regulated neutralization procedure.

matrix.description: Caustics react with halogenated organics (e.g., Dichloromethane, Chloroform) via base-catalyzed dehydrohalogenation. Can produce toxic carbenes, phosgene gas traces, or spontaneous explosion under warm conditions.
matrix.segregationAction: Never pour halogenated extraction solvents into caustic scrubbers or basic waste drums. Route to Dedicated Halogenated Organic Waste container.

matrix.description: Contact between strong oxidizers and flammable solvents provides an immediate oxidizer-fuel pair, causing rapid spontaneous ignition, flash fires, or detonation.
matrix.segregationAction: Store oxidizers in dedicated oxidizer safety cabinets with at least 20 feet separation or fireproof partitions from flammable solvent stores. Never co-dispose into solvent drums.

matrix.description: Extremely vigorous redox reaction resulting in rapid decomposition, thermal shock wave, and toxic gas release.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in physically isolated hazard compartments. Never mix residues in laboratory disposal containers.

matrix.description: Strong oxidizers rapidly oxidize primary and secondary alcohols to aldehydes, carboxylic acids, and CO2 with high heat release and flash fire potential.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate alcohols into standard organic waste; oxidizers to designated heavy metal/inorganic oxidizer waste.

matrix.hazardTitle: Oxidative Amine Cleavage & Toxic NOx Liberation
matrix.description: Oxidation of amines produces toxic nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2), carcinogenic nitrosamines, and extreme reaction heat.
matrix.segregationAction: Isolate oxidizer waste from amino acids, peptide reagents, and amine solvent drums.

matrix.description: Acidification of cyanides immediately releases volatile, lethal Hydrogen Cyanide gas, which inhibits cellular cytochrome c oxidase and causes fatal hypoxia within minutes.
matrix.segregationAction: CRITICAL: Cyanide solutions must be maintained at pH > 11 at all times. Store in locked toxic poison cabinet. Segregate rigorously from all acids.

matrix.description: Acids protonate sulfides to release poisonous H2S gas with rotten egg odor followed by rapid olfactory paralysis and systemic asphyxiation.
matrix.segregationAction: Maintain sulfide waste in basic conditions (pH > 10). Separate from all mineral and organic acid storage areas.

matrix.description: Aqueous dilution does NOT eliminate antineoplastic toxicity. Discharging cytotoxic drugs (Cisplatin, Doxorubicin, Fluorouracil) into water/sewer violates EPA Clean Water Act and kills sewage biomes.
matrix.segregationAction: MANDATORY: USP <800> compliance requires routing all antineoplastic solutions into rigid Yellow Cytotoxic Biohazard Buckets for high-temperature incineration at 1100°C. Never pour down sinks.

matrix.description: Combining cytotoxic active pharmaceutical ingredients with flammable solvents creates dual-hazard regulated waste requiring specialized licensed disposal.
matrix.segregationAction: Label container clearly as 'Dual Hazard: Cytotoxic & Flammable Solvent'. Secure inside secondary steel containment and route to licensed hazardous waste incinerator.

matrix.description: Heavy metal antineoplastics mixed with chlorinated solvents complicate waste incineration and thermal destruction monitoring.
matrix.segregationAction: Segregate into 'Halogenated Cytotoxic Waste' container with explicit manifest tracking per USP <800> & RCRA Subpart P.

matrix.description: Alcohols and non-halogenated organic solvents are mutually miscible and do not exhibit dangerous chemical reactivity, but share high vapor pressure and flammability.
matrix.segregationAction: Co-storage permitted in Non-Halogenated Organic Solvent carboy/drum. Must be grounded and bonded during transfer to eliminate static sparks.

matrix.hazardTitle: Halogenated Dilution & Incinerator Acid Gas Scrubber Requirement
matrix.description: Mixing halogenated solvents (e.g. DCM) into standard flammable solvents contaminates the solvent recovery stream, causing hydrochloric acid gas formation during combustion which corrodes standard incinerator linings.
matrix.segregationAction: Keep Halogenated waste (>0.5% Cl) in a dedicated Halogenated Drum to avoid massive penalty fees and processing surcharges from waste disposal facilities.

matrix.description: Concentrated mineral acids (especially sulfuric acid) can violently dehydrate alcohols into flammable alkene gases or ethers with significant heat generation.
matrix.segregationAction: Dilute solutions before mixing; do not co-store concentrated mineral acids with large alcohol volumes.

matrix.description: Organic peroxides are shock, friction, and heat-sensitive oxidizers. In the presence of flammable vapors, explosive detonation and violent combustion can occur spontaneously.
matrix.segregationAction: Store in explosion-proof, temperature-controlled refrigerator (-20°C). Segregate from solvents. Test periodically for peroxidic crystallization.

matrix.description: Water reduces flashpoint hazards of water-miscible solvents (e.g., Ethanol, Isopropanol) without dangerous reactivity.
matrix.segregationAction: Aqueous-solvent blends can be collected in solvent recovery drums if solvent concentration > 20%, or directed to pre-treatment if biodegradable.
